turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay, so the client wants customers to save shipping addresses for future orders.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Got it. Just to confirm, only logged-in customers can save an address, right?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: That's right. Guest users can't save addresses.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Okay. Can customers save more than one address?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes, they can save multiple addresses.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: And can they choose one as their default address?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Exactly. The default address should be selected automatically during checkout.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: So, if I understand correctly, the customer doesn't have to select an address every time.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Right. The default one will be selected for them.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Okay. Can they change the selected address before placing the order?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes, they can choose another saved address.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: And what happens if they don't have any saved addresses?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: They'll need to enter a new shipping address manually.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Got it. Does that also apply to guest users?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yes. Guests have to enter their address manually.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Okay, so logged-in customers can save multiple addresses, while guests can only enter an address during checkout.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Exactly.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: And the default saved address is selected automatically, but customers can change it before placing the order.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: That's correct.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Great. That sounds clear from the QA side.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Alright. I think we're on the same page now.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Perfect. I'll update the ticket with these rules.
